title: IES Sor 4 sorghum (IES Sorghum 4): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: IES Sor 4 sorghum: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: IES Sor 4 sorghum is a sorghum variety. About 99 days to harvest, 6.2 t/ha in trials. See its ratings and traits. Compare it with others.
excerpt: IES Sor 4 is a registered sorghum variety, also sold or known as IES Sorghum 4 or Ilagan sorghum. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council (NSIC) in 1996 as NSIC 1996 Sg 03. Ilagan Experimental Station DA Region II bred it. It takes about 99 days from planting to harvest, with 6.2 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for IES Sorghum 4 or Ilagan sorghum, this is the same sorghum. The facts below come from the NSIC registry kept by the Bureau of Plant Industry, with notes from its seller and farm sources. Compare it with the others in our [sorghum variety finder](/crop-varieties/sorghum), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for corn and grains](/land-preparation/corn-land-preparation).

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

IES Sor 4 sorghum takes about 99 days from planting to harvest. That is 4.2 days faster than the average of the 3 sorghum varieties with a day count, 103.2 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 6.2 t/ha beats the average of its group, 5.07. It sits in the top quarter of its group. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing. Its seller gives about 99 days.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in the registry trials, rated under natural field conditions

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings on record. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain or pest population comes, so keep scouting. Read up on [Northern corn leaf blight](/diseases/northern-corn-leaf-blight), [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose).

The pests and diseases that hit sorghum fields most often: [Rice birds (maya)](/pests/rice-birds), [Asian corn borer](/pests/asian-corn-borer), [Corn downy mildew](/diseases/corn-downy-mildew), [Corn earworm](/pests/corn-earworm), [Corn planthopper](/pests/corn-planthopper). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Where:** Can be grown anywhere in the country.
Highly resistant to leaf blight, Helminthosporium leaf spot and anthracnose in trials.
Grain sweet enough to eat as food.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: one of only a few sorghum varieties on the NSIC registry, the highest yielding of them. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant IES Sor 4 sorghum
It is recommended for the dry season. Sorghum stands drought better than corn, so it fits the dry season and dry uplands. Pick by use: grain for food and feed, or sweet sorghum for juice and syrup.

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is IES Sorghum 4 the same as IES Sor 4?
items.a: Yes. IES Sorghum 4 is another name for IES Sor 4, registered as NSIC 1996 Sg 03. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes about 99 days from planting to harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 6.2 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of IES Sor 4?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
